after: ## Structure of the atmosphere (4.1.1 a and b)
alt: A schematic column, not to scale. From the surface up: troposphere, where we live and almost all weather happens; stratosphere, with the ozone layer in its lower part absorbing much of the Sun’s ultraviolet radiation; mesosphere; and thermosphere, the highest of the four.
caption: Troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere: the ozone layer is in the lower stratosphere.

alt: A schematic graph of summer temperatures over many years. Each dot is one year’s weather and jumps up and down; one very hot summer is weather. The trend line through them, rising over decades, is a change in climate. Climate is the weather conditions in a location based on the weather over many years.
caption: One hot summer is weather; a rising average over decades is a change in climate.

alt: A schematic cross-section. 1: solar radiation passes through the atmosphere. 2: some is absorbed by land and oceans, heating the Earth. 3: some is reflected back to space by clouds and light surfaces. 4: heat given off by the surface is absorbed by greenhouse gases and clouds and re-emitted back to the surface. 5: this keeps the Earth warm enough for life, about 15 °C instead of about −18 °C.
caption: Pass through, absorb, reflect, absorb and re-emit, warm enough for life: one mark per step.

alt: A pie chart of clean air: nitrogen 78% (about 281°), oxygen 21% (about 76°) and other gases 1% (about 4°), using 3.6° per 1%. In a 500 cm³ sample there are 390 cm³ of nitrogen, 105 cm³ of oxygen and 5 cm³ of other gases.
caption: Each 1% is 3.6°: nitrogen 281°, oxygen 76°, other gases 4°.

alt: Three panels explain arrow types. Reflection: arrows bounce off clouds or ice. Absorption: arrows end at the ground or sea. Absorption and re-emission: arrows leave the surface and turn back from the greenhouse gas layer. Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit heat rather than reflect it; roughly 30% of incoming solar radiation is reflected overall.
caption: Bounce off = reflected; end at the surface = absorbed; turn back from the gas layer = re-emitted.
